key_insight: SurgTEMP introduces a temporal-aware VQA model that uses a text-guided visual memory to retrieve and aggregate relevant frames over time, enabling better, knowledge-driven answers for laparoscopic cholecystectomy videos.
problem_solved: Current surgical VQA methods analyze isolated frames and miss long-range temporal context and task-specific cues in low-contrast, knowledge-heavy laparoscopic videos; SurgTEMP addresses temporal reasoning and targeted retrieval of relevant visual evidence for accurate QA.
method: Temporal-aware video encoder that models long-range dependencies across video frames (e.g., temporal attention/transformer backbone).
Text-guided visual memory: a question-conditioned memory module that stores and retrieves salient visual features across the video to focus on temporally relevant segments.
Multimodal fusion and answer decoder that combines retrieved visual memory with language features for knowledge-driven answer prediction.
impact: Provides a practical architecture for robust temporal and multimodal reasoning in long surgical videos, improving VQA reliability for education and intraoperative support; the text-guided memory idea generalizes to other long-form video QA and domain-specific multimodal tasks.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing video frames with temporal attention weights highlighting relevant segments for a sample question.
Block diagram of the model: video encoder → text-guided visual memory (store/retrieve) → multimodal fusion → answer head.
Before/after example: same question answered using single-frame VQA vs. SurgTEMP with annotated frames and correct answer.
Bar chart comparing qualitative performance or robustness metrics (temporal reasoning, retrieval accuracy) against static-frame baselines.
paper_title: SurgTEMP: Temporal-Aware Surgical Video Question Answering with Text-guided Visual Memory for Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
paper_authors: Shi Li, Vinkle Srivastav, Nicolas Chanel, Saurav Sharma, Nabani Banik
